system_description.narrative_title: State-linked cyber operations escalate geopolitical and economic risk
system_description.narrative_summary: A surge in cyber intrusions and infrastructure attacks—many attributed to state-linked groups (China, Iran, Russia-linked actors)—is reshaping geopolitics, corporate risk, and policy responses. As attacks hit governments, critical infrastructure, and major firms, the open system exchanges digital-attack inputs (malware, exploited supply chains, AI tools) for outputs (data theft, service outages, market losses), producing feedbacks in the form of defensive counter-operations, stricter supply-chain rules, and accelerated military and diplomatic alignment. Drivers include state geopolitical competition, commercially available offensive tooling (including AI), and interconnected global supply chains; responses span law enforcement takedowns, legislative/military spending moves, and corporate cyber hardening.
system_description.scope: State-linked and state-exploited cyber operations and defenses; targeted sectors (government agencies, critical infrastructure, healthcare, transport, telecoms, industrial/IT suppliers); private tech firms and security vendors; intelligence and law-enforcement actions; policy and market reactions (regulation, supply-chain security, stock impacts); enabling technologies (AI, compromised hardware/routers).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitics and international political-economy (security, trade, energy, and technology competition).
adjacent_subsystems: Conventional and regional military/security competition (Taiwan, Korean peninsula, South/SE Asia)
Global trade and supply chains (EU-China trade, manufacturing, telecom supply security)

variables.name: Rate of state-linked cyber attacks
variables.description: Frequency of cyber intrusions and attacks attributable to state-linked actors per unit time across targeted sectors.

variables.name: Offensive cyber capability level
variables.description: Aggregate technical sophistication, tools, personnel, and operational capacity available for offensive cyber operations.

variables.name: Availability of commercial offensive tools
variables.description: Accessibility and market prevalence of off-the-shelf or commercially available offensive cyber toolsets and exploit kits.

variables.name: AI-enabled attack enhancement
variables.description: Extent to which artificial intelligence and automation increase the scale, speed, or sophistication of cyber operations.

variables.name: Interconnected supply-chain complexity
variables.description: Degree of interdependence and technical complexity in global digital and hardware supply chains relevant to cyber risk.

variables.name: Prevalence of compromised hardware
variables.description: Proportion of deployed hardware and networking components in supply chains that are insecure, backdoored, or otherwise compromised.

variables.name: Detection and attribution capacity
variables.description: Capability to detect intrusions, attribute them to specific actors, and produce actionable forensic intelligence.

variables.name: Corporate cyber hardening investment
variables.description: Aggregate level of private-sector investment and implementation in cyber defenses, incident response, and resilience measures.

variables.name: Law-enforcement and disruption effectiveness
variables.description: Effectiveness of disruptive actions (takedowns, arrests, legal actions) against malicious cyber networks and infrastructure.

variables.name: Regulatory and policy stringency
variables.description: Intensity and enforceability of laws, regulations, and policy measures governing cyber security, supply chains, and incident reporting.

variables.name: Military and diplomatic alignment intensity
variables.description: Degree of coordinated military, diplomatic, and strategic alignment among states in response to cyber threats and coercion.

variables.name: Market sensitivity to cyber incidents
variables.description: Degree to which financial markets, investor valuations, and corporate credit are affected by cyber incidents and disclosures.

variables.name: Public and market perceived cyber risk
variables.description: Level of perceived cyber threat among the public, customers, and investors influencing behavior and trust.

variables.name: Service outage duration and severity
variables.description: Average duration and severity (scope of services affected) of outages caused by cyber incidents over time.

variables.name: Volume of data exfiltrated
variables.description: Amount of sensitive or proprietary data exfiltrated through cyber incidents per unit time.

variables.name: Economic loss rate from cyber operations
variables.description: Monetary value of economic losses (direct and indirect) attributable to cyber operations per unit time.

catalysts.title: Xi's Washington visit and US–China meetings
catalysts.description: High-level meetings around Xi's Washington visit that could shift diplomatic posture, joint statements, or reciprocal pressure on cyber norms and responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Trump ratchets up rhetoric... officials meet for Xi's Washington visit' — could alter alignment, policy tone, and perceived risk.

catalysts.title: Xi attends SCO summit
catalysts.description: Xi's participation at the SCO summit may reinforce regional alignments and joint stances that affect state strategic coordination, including cyber posture.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'China's Xi to attend SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan' — likely to shape regional alignment dynamics.

catalysts.title: Major tech companies' defensive surge
catalysts.description: Industry-led push for stronger defenses, information-sharing and tooling aimed at countering AI-enabled attacks and hardening infrastructure.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Major tech companies call for defensive surge to defeat AI-driven hacks' — will drive investment and detection efforts.

catalysts.title: Continued US/FBI takedowns and disruptions
catalysts.description: Sustained law-enforcement operations and court actions targeting state-linked or affiliated hacking networks, and follow-on disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'FBI Shuts Down Sprawling China-Linked Hacking Network'; 'US says it disrupted Chinese hacking operation' — signals more disruptions.

catalysts.title: Additional backdoor disclosures in Zbtlink routers
catalysts.description: Ongoing disclosures and research revealing backdoors in Chinese-made networking hardware, prompting vendor notices, audits, and procurement responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Researchers discover additional backdoors in Chinese-made Zbtlink routers' — will raise measured prevalence and regulatory attention.

catalysts.title: Rapid criminal adoption of AI attack tools
catalysts.description: Wider and faster uptake of AI-assisted tools by criminal and state-linked groups, increasing scale and sophistication of intrusions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies' — shows criminal AI adoption.

catalysts.title: UK tightens supply-chain security
catalysts.description: Regulatory and procurement changes in the UK to harden digital and hardware supply chains following Iran-linked incidents, with implementation activity.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'UK seeks to tighten security of supply chains after Iran-linked cyber attack' — implies regulatory action and procurement changes.

catalysts.title: Taiwan crackdown on AI server smuggling
catalysts.description: Prosecutions and enforcement against illicit AI server trafficking that may disrupt shadow hardware channels and trigger tighter export/supply rules.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'AI Server Smuggling: Taiwan Charges Nine' — enforcement likely to disrupt illicit hardware flows.

catalysts.title: Healthcare sector response to Boston Scientific attack
catalysts.description: Ongoing incident response, regulatory inquiries and sector-wide remediation driven by the Boston Scientific outage will prompt investment and scrutiny.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Boston Scientific hit by cyberattack... global outage' and related reporting — will drive sector responses and investor sensitivity.
